Woman Hacked to Death.
Murphysboro, Ill., July 31.—Mrs. James H. Martin, 45 years old, wife of a lawyer of Murphysboro, was beaten and hacked to death with a hatchet in her home here late today. Following the discovery of her body, Joe Deberry, a negro house servant, whose parole from the state reformatory Mrs. Martin was instrumental in getting recently, was arrested. Later when a mob of 500 men was forming near the jail the sheriff spirited the prisoner away for safe keeping.

NEW MOB
Is Forming to Attack Jail and Lynch Negro Suspected of Murder of Woman.
BY ASSOCIATED PR

HARRISBURG, Ill., July 31—Reports reached here late tonight that a new mob was forming at a town near here today to attack the Harrisburg jail and lynch Joe DeBerry, the negro arrested yesterday on suspicion of having murdered Mrs. J. H. Martin. An extra guard was stationed at the jail. A coroner's jury today returned a verdict holding De Berry for the murder.

Paroled Convict Murders One Who Freed Him—Mob Storms Jail.

Murphysboro, Ill., Aug. 2.—Mrs. James H. Martin, wife of one of the most prominent attorneys in southern Illinois, was murdered Friday afternoon with an ax. A former negro servant who was sent to the state reformatory by the Martins for a theft and who was paroled a short time ago through the efforts of Mrs. Martin, was arrested. A mob began to gather before the county jail and the sheriff hurried his prisoner out of town in an automobile to forestall a lynching.

The crime was committed in the Martin homestead, the woman being found by servants with her head split open. The discovery was made about five o'clock.

Victim His Benefactress.

The authorities immediately began a search for Joe Deberry, a negro who formerly was employed by the Martins. He was convicted of stealing a diamond ring and sentenced to three years in the reformatory at Portiac. He was paroled three months ago through the influence brought to bear by Mrs. Martin. Since his return here he frequently expressed his bitterness toward the Martins for sending him to prison in the first place, and threatened to "get even." He seemed calloused toward the woman who had befriended him.

The negro was found near his home an hour after the murder became known. He was hustled to the county jail, persons who had learned of the killing following the sheriff and threatening the prisoner.

Big Mcb Storms Jail.

Hardly had the news of the crime—which was the second of its kind here in a week—been circulated than a mob formed and stormed the jail.

Sheriff White, anticipating such a demonstration, managed to get the negro into an automobile which he ordered speeded for Marion, the county seat of Williamson county. Ringleaders followed in twelve automobiles and quickly raised another mob at Marion

Again Deberry was taken from jail, and this time the party went to Harrisburg. The mob followed and the Harrisburg jailer refused to accept the negro.

Eluding the crowd, the officials went to Mound City, where Deberry was placed in jail.

Negro Burned to Death.

Temple, Tex., Aug. 2.—Will Stanley, a negro arrested on a charge of murdering three children in this city last Wednesday night, was taken from jail at midnight and burned on the public square in the presence of hundreds of men, women, boys and girls, who cheered as the victim went up in smoke.

When Stanley was cast into the flames he struggled frantically to escape, but was repeatedly shoved back.

Several men said Stanley confessed that he did the killing, claiming he had been hired to do the deed. He begged to be permitted to live long enough to tell all about it, but his alleged admission of guilt was all-sufficient for those around the fire.

The crime for which Stanley lost his life was the slaying of three children, a criminal attack on their mother and physical attack on their father.

Wednesday night the negro entered the house of W. R. Grimes and with a combination spikemail and rail cutter beat the children to death, attacked their father and mother. Neither Grimes nor his wife have recovered sufficiently to give an account of the affair. Grimes still is in a semi-conscious state, and his wife is in a critical condition.

Mutterings of Lynching.
MURPHYSBORO, Ill., Aug. 30.—Repeated threats of lynching today caused a close guard kept around the jail here where Joe Deberry, a negro, was to be tried today for the murder of Mrs. J. H. Martin, wife of a prominent lawyer, who himself died from the shock, following his wife's death.
Deberry was rushed here at midnight, escorted by state troops when a mob of several hundred gathered around the jail at Harrisburg, Ill., and demanded that Deberry be turned over to them. He was taken out by a ruse and brought here by train. A crowd of a hundred met his party at the depot, but aside from mutterings of lynching, made no attempt to molest the prisoner. Three companies of Illinois state militia will guard Deberry while on trial.

NEGRO SLAYER SENT TO ROPE
Murphysboro, Ill., Aug. 31.—Joe Deberry, the negro who murdered Mrs. Elizabeth Martin in her home here July 30, was sentenced to hang October 16, by Judge D. T. Hartwell of Marion, in court here late Monday afternoon.

Deberry went on trial this morning before a special term of court, Judge Hartwell presiding. In his fourth plea of guilty during the course of the day, Deberry stated:

"I killed her for 50 cents. It was premeditated. I went upstairs with a poker to kill Mrs. Martin. You can do with me what you want to."

The court prior to passing sentence referred to his career as prosecutor and judge, and characterized Deberry's crime as the worst in his knowledge.

Hundreds of court-goers and more hundreds of people on the streets cheered repeatedly when sentence was passed.

The Chicago Tribune, a copperhead paper of the middle West, has been busy assailing the South on account of the murder of Leo M. Frank at the hands of a mob. We wonder what the dear old Trib. will say today when it hears of the trouble at Murphysboro, Ills., where three companies of State militia are guarding a gentleman of color from the dear citizens of Illinois.

We submit that if it is wrong for poor benighted, ignorant, degraded, Southern po' whites to engage in lynching, it is far worse for the noble, enlightened, splendid citizenship of the grand old State of Illinois, home of the virtuous and immaculate Tribune which, as a mentor of the morals of the people, has lifted Illinois above excitement, out of hatred and into a sphere of self-control that is beautiful.
